utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. We shall resume this afternoon the evidence of Dragan Zivaljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zivaljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis, will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you gave at the very beginning of your evidence continues to apply to your evidence today until it's complete. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Welcome back, Colonel. Last week, you spoke of an action that some of your units engaged in in the Podujevo, area or actually in the Palatna village area in May of 1999. We looked at an order that provided tasking for some of those units, and you pointed out to us that there was a reference in that order to JSO, but you thought that was a mistake because you believed it was the SAJ that took part in that action. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. I think it had to do with the SAJ rather than the JSO, and that was the mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And I would have you take a look now at Exhibit 5D1070. I can hand you a hard copy. This is a combat report dated the 25th of May from Colonel Gergar about that action in the general area of Palatna, and he says that his brigade units were engaged in providing support to MUP and SAJ forces. So that seems to be consistent with your memory that it was the SAJ rather than the JSO that was engaged there and then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall who the commander of the SAJ forces engaged in that action was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of the SAJ forces was Zivko Trajkovic; however, I don't remember. He was injured by a mine near the village of Bradas. I don't remember now whether he had been injured before -- before. I can't remember who the commander then, though, who stood in for him in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who his deputy was in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, a gentleman by the name of Stalovic [phoen], as far as I can, remember was the deputy, and there was an assistant commander, Zoran Simovic. I assume that it was one of the two who was in the area. That's my assumption. I cannot make any assertions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let me move then to another document. You were asked about this last week, it's Exhibit 5D506, and I'll trade you hard copies with the help of the usher. This is another VJ combat report, and this one is from the commander of the 354th. It's dated the 27th of April, and you were asked about this one. There's a reference to -- I think it's in paragraph 3(b), where it says: "The redeployed units of PJP are in our unit's zone of responsibility and they are not complying with the orders and decisions of the Podujevo Crisis Staff." And you said, at page 24832, last week you thought this comment was arbitrary, but I want to ask you a specific question: Do you know what orders and decisions of the Podujevo Crisis Staff that refers to? Do you know what kind of orders or decisions the Podujevo Crisis Staff was issuing around April 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can talk about the time after that. It was afterwards that I found out. This document was signed by Radosavljevic. I barely know the gentleman. Perhaps I met him only once or twice in the area. I know Mihajlo Gergar better who was the commander of another combat unit. Later on, I heard that, in the municipality of Podujevo, they had set up some kind of a Crisis Staff after the state of war was declared. So I'm aware of that detail, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you some of these questions first. So were you aware in April 1999 that there was a Crisis Staff in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, sometime in mid-April or around the 20th of April, there was resubordination, and then the army took upon itself a more organized role. I assume that it was then that they established the Crisis Staff too. Of course, I joined in these activities. Everything that the army ordered I implemented directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know who was on the Crisis Staff in Podujevo? Do you know any of the people by name or by position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume - well, I am not aware of the exact list - but I perhaps heard that it was Gergar Mihajlo; I assume that this Mr. Radosavljevic was there, too; and some members of the municipal administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you attend any meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed up later at one of the meetings, but I did not know that that had been established at first. But, later on, I showed up at one of the meetings and we discussed the civilians, who at that time were supposed to be deployed, or rather, to be sent back to the places that they had fled from. So it is in relation to these activities that I joined in; and, later on, I saw these people more often?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The meeting that you attended, do you recall when that was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to link this meeting to the return of civilians, after the civilians were on the move, when we talked about the return of civilians to Podujevo. So it is only that date that I could link it up to. If you allow me, I can find it somewhere. In my statement, I can find that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me move on to something else, and then maybe we'll come back to it or Mr. Lukic will address it with you. The return of civilians, are you talking about Kosovo Albanians or Serbians or both?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, Podujevo, for the most part, was populated by a majority Albanian population. There were few percentage points of non-Albanians. I believe that the Albanian people were a majority there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In an earlier answer today, you talked about, I guess, after the 20th of April, you said: "Everything that the army ordered I implemented directly." Why did you do that? Did someone tell you that you were now subordinated to the army and you should do what they ordered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, since excerpts from the map were done by the army and I came there to implement the tasks that were envisaged in these excerpts, I carried out those tasks that had been envisaged there, in those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll come back to that in a little bit, Colonel, but let me continue on following my notes for now. Let me see if I can find another exhibit. This is 5D436, and in a minute I'll hand you a hard copy, but I'll tell you that this is another VJ document. It's a report about an inspection tour, and let me hand you this hard copy in exchange for that one. I think you were shown this when you testified last week, and it's a report by General Velickovic about his tour of the 354th Brigade. And if you could look at item number -- well, it's heading number 3 and then it's item number 9 under number 3. It's on page 5 of the English but I'm not sure what page it is in your B/C/S. I didn't mark that. Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I found it. Point 9, page 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, it says: "There's no single command in the zone of responsibility of the brigade." Is that the first sentence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the zone of responsibility of the brigade, there is no singleness of command." Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question had to do with the next sentence. It said the brigade commander had dissatisfaction with the conduct of the PJP which didn't respect agreed times and axes of engagement. Were you aware of any problem or failure on the part of the PJP to not respect agreed times and axes of engagement with the 354th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer has to be a bit extensive. On that previous day, I gave an answer to that question. I don't know who put it. This is completely incorrect. I had barely seen this gentleman, perhaps once or twice down there, and I had very little cooperation with him. For the most part, I cooperated with Mihajlo Gergar, Colonel Gergar; and, also, there is a reference here to the PJP often resorting to looting, which is totally improper. Also, there is a reference to the great dissatisfaction of soldiers over the fact that the MUP units are better equipped. Look at the argument he provides in relation to their units, the equipment with communications and protection commitment. Well, look, if he did notice that some crimes were being committed, he should either have taken measures or told me about it. He shouldn't have concealed it, not reporting a crime is a crime in our country, in Serbia, and we did take many measures against policemen who had abused their positions. I think that these arguments are completely out of order and wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That was a long answer. Let me ask you a few questions to follow up. Do you know were there, other than your PJP units from the 122nd, were there other PJP units that worked with the 354th Brigade during the war prior to late May 1999. Is it possible he might be referring to some units other than yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, the SAJ unit was engaged; and, at one point, facing Bajgora the JSO was involved. And in view of the fact that the area of Podujevo is near Serbia, we had incursions by smaller groups from Serbia that took advantage of the fact that they were so nearby; and they would engage in crime, looting, et cetera, so we had sears problems with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But he seems to be talking particularly about the PJP, not about the SAJ or the JSO. Were there any other PJP units that were engaged with the 354th, or was it exclusively personnel from your 122nd?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Podujevo is an area that belongs to the broader area of metropolitan Pristina. There was a PJP unit there, the 124th; and from time to time, they were engaged for some work. I don't have a list of such engagements, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also took issue with this complaint about looting, and I know last week you were also shown a document that was written by General Lazarevic in late May 1999, where he was complaining about the MUP committing crimes, not just looting but more serious crimes as well. You can't speak for all police personnel, right? You only have knowledge about your units and those people that you were working side by side with, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Likewise, I state with full responsibility that there is even a mention there of murders and rapes. So I claim with full responsibility that, as for my knowledge, I was not aware of any murder or any rape. As for some serious crimes, we did take measures and these persons were brought into custody. These were policemen that we brought to justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think you told us last week that you prosecuted -- your command prosecuted over 70 cases of abuse. What were most of those 70 cases, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I gave the figure of 70 as an approximate figure. I'm not sure whether it's 67, 68, 72, 75, et cetera; however, in paragraph 18 of my statement, I describe a few cases when we filed crime -- criminal reports against regular policemen from our unit who used their official position as policemen and robbed an Albanian family. I can give you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, we have the statement. Thank you. Let me ask you about call-signs. You mentioned that you think your radio call-sign in 1999 was Lazar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you were in Kosovo in 1998, do you recall what call-sign your unit had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came, I think it was Bor and then another one, and then, ultimately, it was Lazar. I cannot say with any certainty when it was that these changes took place. It's been such a long time, too long a time for me to be able to state anything specific now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You were asked about your participation in an action called Drenica 1. I think that's the one that's reflected in Exhibit 6D712. You said you didn't personally participate in that one but that your deputy Nikolic did. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when you returned to your location, he told you about a problem that had occurred. He complained about the way he had been treated, I guess, by the VJ. Where were you on that occasion? Why weren't you involved in that action? Where were you and what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the area of Podujevo. A smaller unit was supposed to provide assistance in that area at that time, Drenica 1; and my deputy went there with two companies, I believe. He reported to the army combat group there, and he joined in the task that he was assigned to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you told us last week, at page 24840, that Nikolic complained when he got there with the two companies the army wanted to assign him to two different axes, and it was difficult. He couldn't do that, and so there was a problem. Did you write any report about what had happened to Nikolic after that? Did you write any report up the chain to complain about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Nikolic came back from that area, as I've already explained - if necessary, I can repeat it - I think that a military combat group had not shown up, the 37th, I believe; and, therefore, he was supposed to be deployed in an area that was too wide for him and his forces. So he complained about their attitude. He carried out all the tasks there in accordance with the command of the military commander who was there. At this moment, I don't know which military commander this was. I think that, in relation to this I complained, but orally, to Obrad Stevanovic when I saw him. So it wasn't on those days but the days after that. When I came across him, I complained about this attitude. I said that this was not fair, and that such things should be avoided in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was that the first extent of your complaint about this, then, was the oral complaint you made to Obrad Stevanovic? You didn't complain to anybody else, either orally or in writing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was topical then, and that is when I stated that to General Stevanovic. I do not recall anything else in relation to that. I do not remember having complained to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to reporting, Judge Bonomy had asked you a question last week, at page 24843. He said: "When you were asked when the action was over, did you write a report to the Joint Command or something?" Then you said: "We just filed a report." "Now, where did you file it?" You said: "Not to the Joint Command. When all activities were completed, I filed a report to the police administration to the MUP in Belgrade." Do you know where that report would be now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know with any certainty. I wrote a brief report, a summary of what it was that I was doing. It is possible that in that report I partly described the problem that you mentioned a while ago, and I sent it to the first administration of the police; that is, an organizational unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. I don't know whether it's still there. I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember did you also copy anyone else on that report, like a SUP chief or the MUP staff or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I did that in Belgrade. The MUP staff remained in Pristina; that is to say, I couldn't have sent anything to them and I did not have an obligation to send that to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mention reporting to Obrad Stevanovic when you would see him. When and how often did you see him in 1999, during the time that you were there? Would you see him once a week? Every day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very seldom. As far as I can remember, I attended perhaps one or two meetings; and he, well, I don't dare say anything specific now, but I don't think that he saw me more than twice in that area of Podujevo. But I did hear that he was on the move from time to time in certain locations in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When Obrad Stevanovic was not around, who did you report to or did you simply not report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not report to anybody. I did not send reports. On this occasion, I said this to Obrad Stevanovic orally, as I said, because I hoped that he would pass that on to the military officers at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So why did you not report? You and your units were engaged in actions in 1999. Were you relying on the VJ to report about what your MUP units had done in those actions or was nobody interested? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, frankly, I wouldn't like to talk about the shortcomings of the organizational aspect of all of this, but I know for sure about the army - they showed this to me - where they submitted reports, documents, to their command. We were not duty-bound, we did not have that obligation; and, on the other hand, we had problems in terms of our capacity to communicate. Soon the bombing started and the communications were severely impaired; and it was very difficult to communicate, especially towards the staff, the MUP, and some other services.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned Friday - and we looked at the dispatch that sent you to Kosovo in March of 1999, and I think that was Exhibit 6D291 - and you've told us that prior to being sent down there in March 1999, you had been there in January 1999. But I think you told us you didn't have a copy of that dispatch that sent you in January 1999, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for January, this is a period that was not included in this dispatch; that is, the period when our forces were reduced in terms of our presence down there. In Decani, I was attached to the SUP to carry out their regular tasks and duties with a small unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And -- but you don't have the document reflecting that dispatch, right? I think you told us you don't have a copy of that one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who sent you that time, was that also General Djordjevic in January 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The January task is something I took over from another person. I think there had been a unit in Decani as early as November and December in shifts. I came there for some 20 to 25 days as part of a shift to work in the background of Decani and the monastery that is there, to assist the SUP of Pec and Decani. There was a dispatch which covered several shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is: Do you recall, did that dispatch originate from Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that Vlastimir Djordjevic sent it to my chief of secretariat, who then conveyed the task to me, or he may have sent it directly; but I do believe that it came from the sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, what about July 1998, you told us that you were sent down to Kosovo in July 1998. Do you have a copy of whatever dispatch or document sent you there at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know who that one came from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the basic rule is that the sector chief appoints and sends people out. As to whether he authorised anyone to draft that dispatch, I don't know, but I was told by my secretariat chief to go and attend to this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. There was -- there were a few questions to you about who your commander was in 1998 and 1999, and you mentioned that you knew until 1997 that Obrad Stevanovic was the commander of the PJP, but you seemed somewhat uncertain about whether he was still in that position in 1998 and 1999 because you mentioned that he had become an assistant minister during that time-period, right? If it was not Obrad Stevanovic, who was it? Who else could it have been?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I knew for a fact that in 1997 he had a decision appointing him as commander; later on, he was appointed assistant minister. I don’t know whether he retained his position of a commander since as the assistant minister, he was in charge of all uniformed police affairs in Serbia, which is one level up or higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. My question is: Do you know who would have been in the level in between his position as an assistant minister and your position as commander of the 122nd Intervention Brigade? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I think the staff, too, was subordinate to that level of control as regards the sector chief and the assistant minister for police affairs; however, I had no obligations towards the staff in the sense of command. It was a consultative or a service sort of relationship in terms of taking care of the wounded, notifying the families of those who had been killed, logistics, and so on and so forth, or perhaps forwarding documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There's just one little error in the transcript I want to clear up with you. It has you down as saying: "I said that, until 1977" Stevanovic was appointed as commander; and later on ..." It was 1997, I think, you told us before; not 1977, but 1997. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, if we could take a look at Exhibit 5D1418.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is one that Mr. Bakrac, the lawyer for General Lazarevic, showed you. 5D1418.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go I think to the second page. I don't have it in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember looking at this one before? I think there were a pair of telegrams, one from you and then one back to you. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page in B/C/S, I think my question pertains to that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I remember correctly, this was on the 26th of May 1999. You told us that this related to a humanitarian action regarding the return of civilians, but doesn't that say in there something about arresting all the men of military age? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this part; but if that was your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that on the previous page? Did I get my pages mixed up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, there was a sentence like that; but, however, I can still reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a part of the correspondence, when my radio man sent it out, we received a reply. I stated that there were some 150 armed combatants of the KLA escorting the refugee groups in front or at the back from Podujevo. We had an exchange of correspondence to see where the refugees should be returned to. The fact that there were around 150 combatants was also mentioned. When we tried to approach the group, fire was opened on my policemen. We couldn't react since we could not open fire at the civilians. Those 150 were not arrested. We had no possibility to do so. They either discarded their weapons and mingled with the civilians or they fled, and this is something we had to live with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So, on that occasion, did you then not arrest anybody, any military-aged men or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one was arrested. We transported a few families, some wounded, there was a woman about to deliver and our assistance was requested to take them to Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would next like to show you an exhibit. That's Exhibit P3130, and I'll hand you a hard copy. This is the minutes of a meeting of the ministry staff for Kosovo held on the 2nd of November, 1998. Am I right, you were not in Kosovo in November 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will ask you a couple questions anyway, just to see if you were aware of this or heard about it either when you returned to Kosovo or in conversations with colleagues in the PJP, because this meeting indicates that the commanders of all the detachments attended. On I think it's the second page of the document you have -- well, wait a second. On the first page you have, let me ask you first about item number 6. It's armoured vehicles and weapons of a calibre greater than 7.9 millimetres must not be moved, engaged, or used without agreement and permission from the staff. Now, prior to this, when you were in Kosovo in July for two or two and a half months, were there any limitations on your use in the PJP of armoured vehicles or weapons of a calibre larger than 7.9 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the PJP did not have -- I can tell you this: There was a police brigade as part of the SUP in brigade, and it had only one armoured combat vehicle. They also had a so-called TAB; I don't know how to explain that. It was inoperative most of the time, and I think they had a Praga dating before World War II, a very old piece. There were very few such pieces at the disposal of the PJP. Save for the regular infantry weapons, we had the odd mortar or so, and that was the only thing that we could have at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about when you returned in -- either in January 1999 or later in March 1999, did your PJP units have any armoured vehicles or weapons larger than 7.9 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period before March we did not have any, for sure, except for the handgun, the official handgun, it was 9 millimetres in calibre. Later on, perhaps during the spring, we received several armoured vehicles from the army. I don't have that list with me; therefore, I cannot be any more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you came back to Kosovo in January 1999 and then again in March 1999, did you in your PJP unit have any dealings with members of the KVM, the OSCE mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. In January, we had cooperation. We had frequent contacts. There was also an incident of sorts in Decani. When there was a shift of policemen, they wouldn't take my word for it, and I asked them to accompany us to see that there was a shift about to take place. As it happened, the Siptar terrorist forces opened fire at the column, and two men from the OSCE were injured on that occasion. I think it was the 14th or the 15th of January in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could turn to the next page, I think it's the following page for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In English, I'm still on page 3 of the document, and I think it's page 4 of the B/C/S in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item number 8, do you see that? It talks about: "In villages with Serbian inhabitants, take additional protection measures ..." Then go down to the next sentence, where it says: "Make sure that Serbs and members of the RPO," translated here as reserve police squads, "do not misuse weapons, let off guns at weddings, et cetera, do not carry weapons or show them in public in the presence of members of the mission." It goes on: "When on guard duty, use one weapon and prevent individuals from bringing in the weapon they have been issued. Tell them not to state the fact that Serbs are armed and to explain this fact, if they must, using the excuse that it is only members of the guard who are armed." Now, when you were back in Kosovo in January and then in March 1999, were you aware of this, that you should try and take steps not to let the KVM mission know that Serbs, and I take this means Serbs other than the VJ and the active-duty police, were armed? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything about the RPO. I'm not familiar with that area, and I have no knowledge of it. While I was in Decani, there were no Serbs in its environs, except for the monastery and the people there. In March when I arrived in Podujevo, there was several Serb houses in Podujevo town itself, not outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last thing I want to ask you about on this document is item number 10, which says: "The MUP staff in Pristina will now take on the role of planning, and the secretariats will have greater independence in carrying out their regular actions or regular duties, tasks, and obligations ..." Then the last sentence says: "Commanders and deputy-commanders will take command of the dispatched units - 'A' units of the PJP - and all units come under the secretariats." What was the situation when you came back to Kosovo in January 1999 and then in March 1999 in terms of the relationship between the PJP and the SUPs? Were the PJPs independent or did they report to the SUPs? How did that work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January, whenever I could, I attended the collegium meetings of the SUPs of Pec and Decani. Daily, I visited the Decani OUP. I had immediate contact with them since we carried out our regular police duties. There were no actions at that time. In March, we had certain things planned but could not see them through, because soon we saw the commencement of air-strikes and we changed our work mode as well as launched different actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let me move on then to another meeting. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is quite an extensive cross-examination. The law of diminishing returns does appear to be setting in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I mean, the last couple of answers really weren't answers that were of any assistance to us at all. The statements are clear in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have about six additional documents I wanted to ask him about. I'll try and be done in 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next one I want to ask you about, Colonel, is Exhibit P1990. This is a MUP staff meeting on the 17th of February. I can hand you a hard copy of this one as well. Do you recall, were you still in Kosovo at this time, in February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was there in January and returned by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall being at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Then let me show you Exhibit P1989, and this one I believe you will be familiar with. I'll hand you a hard copy of this one. This is from the 4th of April, 1999. This is a meeting of the senior police officials in Kosovo and Metohija with the chiefs of the SUPs and the detachment commanders, and it also lists the SAJ and JSO commanders, General Stevanovic and General Lukic. Do you recall this meeting? You're mentioned on page 3 as having spoken.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I remember being at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you see on page 3 - that's page 3 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S - you mention that the task has been fully completed. The territory is under control. You say refugees were going towards Medvedja? Where is Medvedja? I couldn't find that on my map. Is that in Serbia or is that in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medvedja is in the direction of Serbia towards Vranje. That would be it more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is it actually in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were these refugees you're referring to, are those Serbian refugees or Kosovo Albanians or both?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with any degree of certainty, but I think they were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You see, right below, there's an entry for Zivko Trajkovic as the SAJ commander; and, below him, Radislav Staljevic the SAJ commander in Pristina; below that, there's an entry translated in English as Milorad Jankovic, JSO commander. Do you remember a JSO commander being at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember him being there, but I do see there is an error. JSO commander is not Jankovic, as stated here, but Lukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we've heard other evidence about the JSO commander being the man that we have called by the nickname Legija. Is that the same person you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so; although, there may have been a Milorad Jankovic standing in, but his name was Milorad Lukovic, a.k.a. Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall if Legija was at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him during that year on several occasions; but if it is in the document, I suppose it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm just trying to figure out if this is a typographical error and it should say Milorad Lukovic, or if there really was somebody named Milorad Jankovic in the JSO that attended this meeting, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Milorad Lukovic, a.k.a. Legija. I don't know any Milorad Jankovic, and I suppose it was a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you next about Exhibit P2011. This is from the 20th of May, 1999, and it's from the Pristina Corps command signed by Colonel Kotur. This is an order for an operation called Sekac. Have you seen this document before coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could look at item number 5.1, I think it's on page 4 of the English and I think it's on page 4 of the B/C/S as well. It's task for units, and item 5.1 is for the 122nd MUP Detachment of a strength of three PJP companies. Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember this action and whether or not parts of your 122nd took part in it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to add something. In that area, it was Bosko Buha who commanded that part of the detachment, and there was his assistant Vladimir Ilic. I wasn't there. This is quite remote from Podujevo, and I have no insight of these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then I just have two final documents I want to ask you about. The first one is Exhibit number 6D1023. I'll hand you a hard copy. This is entitled: "Joint forces engagement plan." Military secret attachment number 2, Pristina Corps command 25 April 1999. Did you see this document before coming into court to testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I know it's a technical point and I know the Prosecution did supplement their list for cross-examination I believe just this morning, but this document was neither on the original list nor on the supplemental list, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was on a supplemental list I received from the Defence as one they were going to use in their direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Colonel, did you hear my question? Did you have a chance to see this document before you came into court to testify?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You'll see there are three headings across the top: Combined operations unit, which list what appear to be VJ units; then there's a column called reinforcements, which have primarily what appear to be either border guard units or military district units and deployed volunteers; and the third column says resubordinated forces executing tasks. Do you see that third column? You'll see, under item number 1 with the 125th Motorised Brigade, that the 122nd Intervention Brigade is listed. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it in item 1, the third column.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Do you recall, in or around the 25th of April, 1999, whether some parts of your 122nd Intervention Brigade were executing tasks with the 125th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was probably the part of the detachment that had to do with Pec, Bosko Buha, because this is something that I'm totally unfamiliar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go to the second page, then, there in the third column, there are four additional references to the 122nd Intervention Brigade. You'll see, item number 7, the 252nd Armoured Brigade. Do you recall, in late April 1999, were elements of the 122nd engaged in tasks with the 252nd?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But in item 10, with the 211th, perhaps I could find activities of the detachment that I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how about under item number 9, with the 15th Armoured Brigade, or item number 12, with the 354th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under number 9, I don't see the 354th. I don't see that written anywhere, and I don't recognise these other units under number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Under number 9, the 15th Armoured Brigade, is the VJ unit.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm unfamiliar with that, too, that which is under number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But number 12, the 354th, that you told us before was a unit that you did have some engagement with, right, because we saw that document where there were complaints about the PJP from the commander in the 354th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I've already answered that question, and then there's the 211th Armoured Brigade that I cooperated with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Did you know Goran Guri Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him. I knew him. I knew Mr. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was his position or what was his job, first of all, in July of 1998, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was appointed as member of the staff for training, the training of PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And how about in 1999, do you know what his position was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he continued with those activities, as far as I know, but I saw him very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I would have some additional questions based on the cross-examination by Mr. Hannis. It only has to do with two topics: The topic of resubordination that was dealt with today and this other topic that I think you were surprised by, too; I mean the answer that was provided on Thursday in relation to that particular order of the Pristina Corps that allegedly the witness received through the MUP staff. So one or two questions respectively with regard to these two subjects. Resubordination, today we heard something completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These arise only if you say that something the witness has said in this cross-examination has adversely affected the case for your Defence; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That is what I say with regard to both matters. They adversely affect our Defence case because it was my understanding that today on page 1 -- on page 5, lines 1 through 5, the witness said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue and let's see what emerges.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zivaljevic, if you remember on Thursday, during my examination and on transcript page 24858, lines 19 through 21, I asked you whether Colonel Gergar had command over you. Your answer was that you would not call that command, that he did not command you, that you only cooperated with him. Immediately after, that on page 24859, lines 1 -- lines 2, 3, 4, I asked you whether at any point in time, in 1998 or in 1999, you were resubordinated to the army and to Colonel Gergar. You said no, quite literally, "no, I only cooperated with him and I listened to his opinions." Today you said to us, on page 5/1, that you came to Kosovo on orders; and when these maps were issued, you were resubordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia. When was it that you were not telling the truth, on Thursday or today?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. If he's going to ask a question, he's going to have to ask a legitimate question, not in that type of form where he's essentially making arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this sort of additional cross-examination should be confined to a very pointed question. Now, what is the question you want to ask? We don't want to hear your arguments at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My question is whether at any point of time you were resubordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia or the commander of the 211th Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one second. Your quotation from today's evidence was that he said he was resubordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia on page 5, line 1. Now, let's look at page 5, line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until 5, Your Honour. Your Honour, it's line 3 -- or rather, 1 through 3, sorry, and 4 and 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Give us a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or rather, 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this isn't a suitable area for further cross-examination by you. The answers that the witness has given we will look at in the overall context and evaluate his evidence. You don't, just because he says something slightly different or in any way different from earlier, automatically have the right to re-cross-examine. That would mean that we would be going back and forward across the courtroom forever. Now, let's hear what your next matter is, but I suspect none of them are appropriate for further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will try, and I hope this will be more appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, on Thursday, you said to us that you received plans --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This isn't the way to go about this. If you have a specific question you want to put that requires to be answered so that you can avoid prejudice, then put it; but don't let's have a narrative of the competing versions of the evidence and then an assertion by you that one or other must be right and the other wrong. That's not the way to do this. It doesn't sound to me as though you are doing anything other than trying to argue a case at this stage, rather than seek answers that will help us to come to an accurate determination of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to show a document and put one single question; after that, I will have no further questions. The document is 6D291. It's a dispatch of the assistant minister, chief of the public security sector, Vlastimir Djordjevic. On several occasions today and earlier on, the witness said that he'd like to have this before him, so I would like to have it displayed to the witness on the screen, and he can tell me then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness had it before him on Thursday, didn't he, and that's the dispatch sending him to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And after that, during the cross-examination by Mr. Hannis on Thursday - that's what I was trying to explain to you - he said that he received orders and maps in an envelope from the MUP staff and that he worked on the basis of this dispatch. He acted on the basis of the dispatch that was sent -- that sent him to Kosovo. So my question is for him to have a look at the dispatch and tell us where there are instructions by the assistant minister telling him that he should act in accordance with military plans. That's my only question, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a situation where the document was available to the Defence of Mr. Lazarevic. I think they even introduced the document or had it on their list. It was used with the witness, and they clearly had an opportunity to present their cross-examination at that point in time. It would appear that they're trying to basically sideline the regular procedures in this case and have a second bite at the apple. I don't think they're permitted. Secondly, if they're going to rely on representations about what the witness did or didn't say in order to try and have a second bite at this apple, I would request that they give precise quotations to the record of all their assertions, as the prior assertion in this case, the transcript page that showed, did not say what they perhaps thought it to say. So I think we should have a full picture if, in fact, they have a grounds for asking further questions at this stage, but I submit they do not insofar as the document was available to them, and this is clearly not something new that has come up to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: More importantly than any of that, the document is there for us to read and to draw our own inferences from the document. So we will not allow further cross-examination on that basis, Mr. Bakrac. Now, Mr. Ivetic, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honour. We still have -- we're going until quarter to in this session; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, I do have some questions arising from your cross-examination these past few days, to clarify some things. First of all, last week, when my colleague Mr. Bakrac asked you about uniforms, this is at the 11th page of that transcript from Thursday, lines 9 through 19, it is recorded as follows. The question was: "Mr. Zivaljevic, could you please be so kind as to tell me the members of your detachments wore what kind of uniforms? "A. Well, it depended on the period, the time-period in which they took part. As far as I can remember, in the period of 1998, for the most part they wore camouflage uniforms for urban actions; that is, the grey-blue camouflage. Towards the end of that year when these uniforms could be issued, then green camouflage uniforms were issued. These were uniforms that were used subsequently after that in 1999. "Q. So you had grey camouflage as well? "A. Before that during 1999, sometime up until the autumn, I cannot say with certainty that it was grey camouflage uniforms." And at paragraph 8 of your statement, you described the uniforms that are worn, and the question I have for you is: What did you precisely mean with the reference to grey-blue camouflage uniforms and grey camouflage uniforms in this exchange with Mr. Bakrac that is recorded in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I meant blue-grey camouflage uniforms. I probably said grey-blue, but it doesn't really make a difference. Blue-grey camouflage uniforms, definitely. Blue-grey camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one other matter came up. Actually, Mr. Hannis also made reference to it. If I was smart, I would have put down the updated translate pages, and inserted lines from the ones that are on my version of LiveNote. But at page 47, at lines 5 through 10, the questioning from the honourable Judge Bonomy, you were asked about the reports, and you said you filed a report to the police administration in the MUP building. The question I have for you is: When did you file this report that you mentioned in response to the Judge's question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all these activities, we submitted a brief report to the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would that have been -- would that have been in the course of the war, before or after the withdrawal? Can you pin it down any more specifically in terms of the time-period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After returning to Belgrade, since we did not have the right conditions, we didn't have an office out in the field, we didn't have the necessary facilities, we went back to Belgrade, we wrote that up, and submitted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That still doesn't answer when, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree, it does not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you -- well, let me try and direct it this way. If we focus on the end of the war, June of 1999, do you know whether this report was authored by you before or after the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume - I don't know the exact date - but I assume that it's in June, the end of June, or perhaps the beginning of July 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Today, Mr. Hannis asked you about Exhibit P3130 and the statement relating to movements of armoured vehicles with guns in excess of 7.9 millimetres. Are you at all familiar with the types of vehicles foreseen for police patrols by the Byrnes-Djordjevic agreement for the time period when the KVM was in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, this is the period from October 1998 until March; is that right? As far as I can remember, since I did spend a shift in Decani, in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Hang on. Stay close to my question. My question is very specific. Are you familiar with the types of vehicles foreseen by -- for police patrols by the so-called Byrnes-Djordjevic agreement for the time-period during the KVM mission in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that agreement exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I just don't have the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So do you need to ask the witness if your point is consistency?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To find out the witness's knowledge so that I can perhaps ask the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does his knowledge matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as the Prosecution asked him what his knowledge was of this particular -- or these particular facts, I think it does matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what he told you was that the detachment from Belgrade was so ill-equipped that it didn't have these vehicles and equipment anyway. However --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if that is the only inference that is presented by the Prosecution from this document, then I don't have any questions, but I suspect it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the role of Mr. Mijatovic from the MUP staff in Pristina vis-a-vis the Kosovo Verification Mission during the time-period it was on the ground over there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give you any comments on that. I am not very familiar with what it was that he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at -- today, at page 19, lines 1 through 4, you were responding to a question posed by Mr. Hannis of whether PJPs were independent or did they report to the SUPs. You said in lines -- page 19, lines 1 through 4: "There were no actions at that time. In March, we had certain things planned but could not see them through, because soon we saw the commencement of air-strikes and changed our work mode as well as launched different actions." When you say you launched different actions, what actions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to Podujevo, an excerpt from the map was waiting for me there, telling me what it was that I was supposed to do there. Actions started, therefore, and I got involved in my work in relation to that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at -- last week, on Thursday, Mr. Bakrac showed you Exhibit P1990, minutes of a meeting at the MUP staff dated the 17th of February, 1999, and he asked you to read the portion of that, wherein it states that the staff is planning to carry out or plans to carry out once ordered actions in the region of Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica. I'd like to take a look at two documents in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First off, if we can have Exhibit Number 4D365.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As you will see, this is a document from the command of the 3rd Army dated the 1st of February, 1999. If we look at item number 5 on the second page, you could read that entire portion to us, so that we're on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it should be the second page of both copies I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, there must be a purpose in this, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a document the witness is familiar with?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It refers to regions that I'm hoping that the witness is familiar with, since the Prosecution asked him about a meeting that he was not present -- pardon me, that Mr. Bakrac asked him about a meeting he was not present for and asked him about actions in a particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to figure out whether the witness has any knowledge of the areas listed in this document because I believe there's a connection I'm about to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, looking at item 5, we have it both on the screen in Serbian and English, so you don't need to read it out loud, but please review it for yourself. We see that the Pristina Corps command is responsible to draft a plan and to ensure coordination with units of the Republic of Serbia MUP for the region Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo. How does this geographical region compare to the area that was the cited in the minutes of the meeting of the MUP staff, which again from the testimony -- from the documents shown to you by Mr. Bakrac has Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. This is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll repel that objection. It's not a leading question. It's a question designed to clarify what may otherwise remain unclear. So you may answer the question, Mr. Zivaljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, the command of the Pristina Corps will draft a plan, and it has to do with the areas of Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo. Lab is Malo Kosovo above Podujevo, except that the name is called differently in one way of speaking and differently in this other way of speaking. There is no further comment that I can make. So I got involved in these tasks in accordance with this. May I add something? I beg your pardon. When I arrived, that task was waiting for me there, and I was carrying out directly work envisaged under this task in the area of Lab or Malo Kosovo. Let me be specific on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can then move, we see from this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we relate that to what is also described as Dragobilje? Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not Dragobilje. Malo Kosovo, Malo Kosovo. Lab or Malo Kosovo, that's the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what region Dragobilje is? Is there another name for the region Dragobilje, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have -- you see that the dead-line for this planning by the Pristina Corps command is the 15th of February, 1999, and if we can look at another document P2808.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it now. I saw it just now. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. You just saw what now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dead-line, that's what you asked me about again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And looking at this document from the Pristina Corps command dated the 16th of February, 1999, for breaking up and destroying the STS in the region of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo; and, again, I ask you to take a -- we have the same -- if we could take a closer look at page 5 of the Serbian, paragraph 5.1, this is the assignments for units. Do you recognise any of the assignments listed herein?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I recognise the unit and that part of the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say you recognise the unit and the part of the task. Do you recognise these as being tasks of a particular unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 5/1 TT 211 from the area of deployment, that pertains to the unit -- excuse me, the unit commanded by Mihajlo Gergar. Kursumlija is the southern-most town in Serbia proper in the direction of Podujevo. Palatna, Kursumlijska, Banja, and so forth, and Luzane, Donja Lapastica, Donja Obranca, that's above Podujevo. I participated in that part according to the task I had. In the second part, where it says "task," it says: "Together, with the forces of the 22nd Detachment of the PJP and the SAJ of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, carry out an attack," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No need for you to read any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we're at the break. I apologise for overriding. I still have a handful of questions, but it will be brief within ten, 15 minutes or so after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say your instructions were awaiting you when you arrived in Podujevo, who did these instructions come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received a map excerpt. When I met with the military group commander Gergar, he explained the task professionally to me, and that was the initial part. After that, I began working on that task directly. I was engaged in that part of the task directly, the task that was envisaged. It is this task that we have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who did you actually receive the map excerpt from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My courier came back with it. I suppose it came through the staff. My courier went there and brought the excerpt back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We need to have a break again at this stage, Mr. Zivaljevic, that will be for 20 minutes. Could you leave the courtroom and we will resume at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, you wanted to raise something in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour. Thank you. It pertains to a matter that's been discussed just recently on the re-direct. It relates to Exhibit P2808, which is the Pristina Corps command document from General Lazarevic dated the 16th of February, 1999, regarding operations in the area of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo. There is a related document. What I'd like is either a brief application asking you if I can ask the witness five questions or suggesting to the Court that you may want to ask him a question about the document. I'm afraid that this witness is in a unique position to address something about this document based on an answer he gave Thursday, when Mr. Bakrac asked him at page 24856, line 21, and for those who don't have the updated it was page 60, line 7 on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC SAID
utterances.text: "So in March you had documentation pertaining to all the actions all the way until the end of June, right, is that what you're trying to tell us?" The answer was: "I want to tell you that I knew about an action which was of a broader spectre, three larger actions pertaining to Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and another action that I can't remember just now. This activity was carried out by the Pristina Corps. They prepared the documentation. I read that documentation." There's another exhibit 6D716. Which was on the notification I received for the 65 ter notification for the witness Adamovic, the next witness to come. I think Friday we asked to get the English translation, because in e-court it was listed as denied for us, not through any fault of the Defence, but apparently there was some glitch, and we were only able to receive it this morning. It is a document dated the 19th of February, 1999, entitled: "MUP staff," unsigned, just listed as the commander, but it is an order to break up and destroy forces of the STS in the sector of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo with specific tasks for specific MUP units. I think this might be the document that this witness said: "I read this documentation." I would either like to ask him that question or ask the Court to show him that document and ask him: Is that the document you read? That's my application, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why was it you didn't raise P2808 in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't think that was what he had seen, because I read 2808 as mostly talking about tasks for VJ units, and I -- I didn't do a very good job of analysing that. I didn't ask him about that. I did get the translation of this this morning, but I didn't make the connection to what he said about having read that documentation until this discussion took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I maybe misunderstood what you're saying here. You're not asking for an opportunity to ask more questions about P2808?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. I think he's been answering questions about that. I just want to ask him about 6D716.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can give some assistance on 6D716.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I note now, pulling this up, I'm surprised to hear Mr. Hannis mention it was entitled "the MUP staff." And pulling up the English translation, it appears that that's what the English translation says. It says the Serbian however, says "komanda MUPa," which I think even for those who don't speak Serbian is the "command of the MUP" or "the MUP command." So I think that should be clear, if, indeed, that is an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you object in the circumstances to Mr. Hannis having an opportunity to ask about 6D716?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's going to open up a whole new area of questioning for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we interrupt your examination for that purpose. Do you object to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No. I mean, I don't know what grounds I would have to object, apart from the fact that he's already had an opportunity to do so and he did have that exhibit. That was one of the exhibits that was on the amended notification for cross-examination. So they had the exhibit, they had the witness, and they didn't ask questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he is saying that he couldn't open that, and it was intimated in relation to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that he was able to open it this morning with the translation, so they've had time. I mean, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, do you oppose Mr. Hannis having the opportunity to ask about 6D716?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not, Your Honour, given that it is a MUP document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In light of what's developed here, I shall ask the witness about 6D716. So he may now return to the court, and while he's returning put 6D716 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, on Thursday, when you were being questioned by Mr. Bakrac, the issue arose of the documentation available to you in March, and he asked you whether you had documentation pertaining to all the actions all the way until the end of June. Your answer was that you knew about an action that was of a broader nature, three larger actions, pertaining to Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and another action that you said you couldn't remember. Now, I want you to look at the document which is in front of you on the screen now, and tell me if that is in any way connected with that answer that you gave on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order, this is a document I cannot -- the header says "MUP command," and it is an order to break-up and destroy forces of Albanian terrorists in the sector of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo. I recognise the parts referred to. Malo Kosovo is north of Kosovo, and then Drenica and Malisevo. But I'm confused by the heading saying "MUP command." I am not familiar with that. The Malo Kosovo action, when I came, that is something I took part in as well. I worked in accordance with the map excerpt that I received via the courier, and the commander of the combat group who awaited me there met me to explain to me the task itself. Following the order he had, I implemented the task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you now look, please, at paragraph 5.1, which is on page 4 of the English. Do you recognise that task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise it. The 22nd Detachment of the PJP, this being the detachment I commanded, from the area of deployment to be brought to the line next to villages Donja Repa, Prepolac, and Donja Lapastica. I recognise the villages mentioned in this task. I also recognise BG 211, the combat group. It says, a pincer attack or enveloping attack should be executed along the axis, so on and so forth. I recognise that detail, as well as the villages referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you remember in what form you received your instructions to undertake that task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the map excerpt on which the axes of units were marked. Mr. Gergar explained, based on the document when I arrived there, all of the axes of movement and the way the task was to be executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when you said on Thursday that you knew about three larger actions and that you read the documentation, can I take it from your answers it wasn't this particular document which is on the screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised the actions, but I did not recognise the detail I referred to from the header of the document, at the very beginning of the document. I'm not familiar with that. However, as for the text, I do recognise that these were the actions I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, do you want to prompt me to ask anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, only perhaps to inquire when he said he read the documentation, whether he was referring only to maps or did he read something additional, if not this document some other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you help us with that, Mr. Zivaljevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely so. I received the map excerpt. The document that the commander of the combat group had had a body of text describing the task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That doesn't quite answer the question. In addition to the map, did you actually receive a document with a body of text on it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, when I arrived in Podujevo, I received a written notification on where the meeting was to be held with the military commander, this being Mr. Mihajlo Gergar and the combat group 211. He organized the briefing at which he explained the task with the details as set out in this document. Now that you have shown me this document, I can tell you that I agree with this part concerning the engagement of forces in item 5, and I recognise all the details. However, I do not recognise the header of the document; that is a discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Bakrac, does that raise any issues for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. You've already asked the witness my first question relating to this document. First of all, I'd like to have the usher's assistance. Maybe this will short-circuit the cross-examination. I'd like to show the witness a copy of P2808 and 6D716 side by side. I have hard copies of those two exhibits. Maybe if we can put one on the ELMO, except that they're in Serbian. Well, that way we can have one on e-court and one on the ELMO for the rest of the persons in the courtroom following.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question is going to be very simple, sir, for the first question at least. The Prosecution has shown you this Exhibit 6D716 purportedly from the MUP command. If we can have you compare the first page of this exhibit with P2808, the order from the Pristina Corps, and if I could just have you make any comment on whether, in fact, the introductory text for these two exhibits --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Objection, Your Honour. We can compare the documents ourselves. The issue at hand is whether the witness ever saw this document and what it is that he can tell us about it. He's not an expert to compare. We can do that for ourselves. We have both the documents in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There seems to be force in that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the point being, though, that in Serbian it may be true; but in English, when translations of two documents are done by two different translators, sometimes there are slight nuances in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's a matter that should be submitted again to CLSS; and if you wish us to do that, we'll do it now. You're concerned about the heading in 6D716?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Aside from that, I'm talking about the text of the first page itself. It's our submission that the text is identical to both the Pristina Corps command and this other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we will note the submission --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and take it into account in due course. Please proceed with questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- that the witness can assist us with from his personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned, sir, that you were unfamiliar with the title of this document, 6D716, which I hope you have in front of you. Did, in fact, any formation or entity ever entitled the MUP command exist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He doesn't have it in front of him at the moment, because we're relying on the screen and it's a different document that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
